research_question: In 2026-2028, is a multi-runtime, push-based 'AI agent team compiler' (DreamTeams thesis) a viable product category against (a) vendor-native crews from Cursor/Anthropic/OpenAI, (b) existing single-agent stores (GPT Store, Claude sub-agents), and (c) framework abstractions (CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph) — and what does prior art for meta-layers (HuggingFace, npm, awesome-lists, Helm, VSCode marketplace) tell us about the win condition?

phases.name: Landscape
phases.objective: Survey the current state of multi-agent team composition and staffing for AI-assisted coding in 2026. Who is shipping 'crews', 'teams', 'agent bundles', or 'team builders'? What does the vendor roadmap look like for Anthropic Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex/Agents, Aider, OpenHands? What does the agent-framework space look like (CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, OpenAI Swarm, Mastra, Google ADK, Microsoft Magnetic-One)?
sub_questions: What 'agent team' or 'multi-agent crew' products exist in 2026 for AI-assisted software development specifically (not generic multi-agent frameworks)?
What have Anthropic, Cursor, OpenAI, and JetBrains publicly said about team/crew/multi-agent roadmaps in the last 6 months?
phases.evidence_priorities: Official product announcements, vendor roadmap blogs, YC/a16z market maps for AI dev tools 2026, public framework comparisons, agent-framework benchmark suites (TAU-bench, SWE-bench Multi-agent, AppWorld), recent papers on multi-agent system composition
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 3+ distinct approaches/products identified spanning vendor-native, multi-vendor, and framework layers

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: How do successful developer-tool meta-layers execute the 'compiler + community curation' pattern? Deep-dive HuggingFace model hub, npm package registry, GitHub awesome-lists, Helm charts, VSCode extension marketplace. What's the recommender mechanic? How does community curation get bootstrapped? What's the install-and-update UX? How does versioning + dependency-resolution work for templates/recipes that bundle multiple primitives (not single packages)?
sub_questions: Across HuggingFace, npm, Helm, awesome-lists, and VSCode Marketplace — what 3-5 mechanics correlate with sustained meta-layer adoption?

How do template-bundle systems (Helm charts, Cookiecutter, create-react-app, Vercel starter templates, dotfile/dotbundle managers) handle the 'compile from inputs → emit a complete spec' UX that DreamTeams proposes?
phases.evidence_priorities: Engineering blog posts from HuggingFace/Vercel/Cursor/GitHub, post-mortems on plugin marketplaces, NPM/HF/VSCode public adoption curves, papers on developer-tool adoption, talks from package-manager maintainers (Cargo, npm, Pypi)
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ concrete meta-layer architectures documented with their adoption + curation mechanics

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: Why have past developer-tool meta-layers failed or stagnated? GPT Store: low engagement after launch hype. Heroku Add-ons: structurally lost market. Atom packages: died with editor. VSCode Tasks templates: never reached HF-level adoption. What does the data say? What are the recurring failure modes for community-curated developer-tool registries? Particular focus on AI-agent-specific failures: prompt-rot, model-version drift, vendor API breaks, composer outputs hallucinating tools that don't exist.
sub_questions: What's the documented adoption arc of GPT Store, Claude sub-agent sharing, Anthropic's Skills, and similar AI-agent meta-layers from launch through 2026?
What are the dominant failure modes for community-curated developer-tool registries (prompt-rot, version drift, abandoned templates, low-quality long-tail submissions)?
phases.evidence_priorities: GPT Store post-launch retrospectives, Hacker News and Reddit threads, vendor disclosures of usage numbers, blog posts critiquing AI agent marketplaces, post-mortems on dead developer tool registries (Heroku Add-ons, Atom)
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 5+ distinct failure modes documented with concrete examples and mitigations

phases.name: Contrarian
phases.objective: Will Anthropic, Cursor, or OpenAI fold the staffing layer into the runtime, making multi-runtime neutrality irrelevant? The DreamTeams brief argues multi-vendor neutrality is a 'structural moat.' Pressure-test this: vendor-native solutions historically win when integration depth matters more than portability (Heroku vs DigitalOcean, VSCode vs Atom, Slack vs Mattermost). Conversely, neutrality wins when standardization is unfinished and lock-in costs are real (Docker vs Pivotal CF, Kubernetes vs ECS, LSP vs editor-specific autocomplete). Which pattern applies to 2026-2028 AI coding tools?
sub_questions: Historically, when has multi-vendor neutrality beaten vendor-native depth in developer tools, and when has it lost? What predicts the outcome?
phases.evidence_priorities: Industry analyst takes (Latent Space, AI Tinkerers, a16z, Stratechery), case studies of meta-layer survival/death, decision frameworks for neutrality-vs-integration tradeoff, recent Cursor/Anthropic/OpenAI announcements about 'crews' or 'multi-agent' features
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive counter-arguments found with historical precedent

agent team compiler dream team AI coding
developer tool plugin marketplace failure modes
vendor-native vs neutral developer tools history
exclusion_criteria: Results before 2024 unless explicitly historical case-study material
Generic 'what is multi-agent AI' overviews — looking for production data, not 101 content
Pure academic multi-agent reinforcement learning research (RoboCup, MARL)

required_output_schema.per_finding_format: Each finding must include: claim, supporting evidence (preferably with quoted snippet), confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), source URLs, and counter-evidence if any
required_output_schema.per_source_format: URL, title, credibility (1-5), recency (publication date if known), type (primary/secondary/opinion)

openai_instructions: Apply fault-tree analysis to the DreamTeams thesis. Build a logical decomposition: for DreamTeams to win, what must be true about (a) vendor behavior, (b) user behavior, (c) the agent ecosystem's fragmentation trajectory, (d) the speed at which Anthropic/Cursor can ship competing crews? For each node, what's the probability and what would falsify it? Focus on edge cases and deductive contradictions.
gemini_instructions: Pull broad data: recent Anthropic/Cursor/OpenAI blog posts (last 6 months), GitHub repos for agent frameworks with star counts and contributor counts, HuggingFace community datasets adoption data, GPT Store published statistics. Extract code/spec examples from CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, OpenAI Swarm to compare how each handles team composition. Synthesize quantitative comparison tables where possible.
claude_instructions: Investigate the contrarian Phase 4 angle most aggressively. Look for thoughtful critiques of the 'meta-layer for AI agents' thesis specifically — not just generic 'AI hype' takes. Cross-verify claims about adoption numbers, vendor roadmaps, and framework comparisons between sources. Where you find numerical disagreements (e.g., one source says GPT Store has X custom GPTs, another says Y), flag them explicitly. Investigate the 'vibe coder' persona — is there real survey data on who they are and how big the population is?
